chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: Fats breaks through: high C, F and beyond
summary: With the new mouthpiece Fats hits high C and F within weeks, and McGhee praises him.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: You knew he was going to develop.

He was going to develop, yeah, because he... He wanted to! You know, when a man wants to do something, he can do it if he tries. All he needs is a percentage(?) to be able to do it. Like, I told him, I said, "Man, you'll be able to do it."

So getting back to the story. After he got the mouthpiece, we were on the road, and maybe the second week after he had this mouthpiece, he hit a high C and it scared him! He said, "Man, did you hear that?" I said, "Yeah, Fats, I heard it." I said, "High-C, I know what you're trying to do." He said, "Look, man, if I can hit high-C, I ought to be able to hit high F." I said, "You try. You'll hit it." And he did. One night he said, "Man, you hear that? That's an F!" I said, "Yeah, I know it's an F, Fats. I've been hearing that for years. I know." He said, "Yeah, but I hit it!" I said, "Yeah, I realize that, too. But that ain't nothin'. You should be able to get a G and a B-flat and an A (?), too." So pretty soon, he was getting to where he could go up there...any time he'd get ready to hit a high note, he would pound one. BANG, it would jump out of that horn, man. It was beautiful, man.
Plus, Fats was such a beautiful cat, he deserved it. I said, "Yeah, Fats, you got it now. You got what you want. So go on about your business." And boy, he was cookin' on
trumpet, too, man. I loved him. I think he was somethin' else.
